S7 Classes for the Method of an Expectation

Source: R/expect_method.R
ExpectMethod.Rd

ExpectMethod is the abstract parent of the objects that select how an expected derivative is obtained. Its three subclasses are ExpectOPG, ExpectIntegrate and ExpectMC. They are built by expect_opg(), expect_integrate() and expect_mc(), which are the functions to call; the classes are exported so that S7::S7_inherits() can test an object. expected_derivative_methods compares the three.

ExpectOPG has no properties. ExpectMC has two, nsim, the number of draws, and identity. ExpectIntegrate has seven, identity and the tolerances and limits of the quadrature and of the series summation (see expect_integrate()). The raw constructors ExpectMC() and ExpectIntegrate() do not validate their properties, whereas expect_mc() and expect_integrate() do.

Usage

ExpectMethod()

ExpectOPG()

ExpectIntegrate(
  identity = "hessian",
  quad_atol = 1e-10,
  quad_rtol = 1e-08,
  max_panels = 4096L,
  series_atol = 1e-12,
  series_rtol = 1e-10,
  max_terms = 100000L
)

ExpectMC(nsim = integer(0), identity = "hessian")

Arguments

identity

One of "hessian" and "score", the identity that the expectation is taken of, for ExpectIntegrate and ExpectMC. It is documented in expected_derivative_methods.

quad_atol, quad_rtol, max_panels, series_atol, series_rtol, max_terms

The properties of ExpectIntegrate that set the quadrature and the series summation, documented in expect_integrate().

nsim

The number of Monte Carlo draws, a single positive number, for ExpectMC.

Value

An S7 object of the class named, which inherits from ExpectMethod.

See also

expected_derivative_methods for the comparison of the three methods; expect_opg(), expect_integrate() and expect_mc() for the constructors.

Examples

a <- expect_mc(nsim = 500)
S7::S7_inherits(a, ExpectMethod)
#> [1] TRUE
S7::S7_inherits(a, ExpectMC)
#> [1] TRUE
a@nsim
#> [1] 500
a@identity
#> [1] "hessian"
